Note::NlpAccessor::expand_contractions¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::NlpAccessor::expand_contractions() const

Make Selected English Contractions Explicit¶

expand_contractions() rewrites common straight-apostrophe English contractions as separate words. It is useful before word counting, rule-based matching, or tokenization when can't should contribute can and not instead of one surface token.

The fixed vocabulary includes can't, won't, I'm, you're, we're, they're, it's, that's, there's, what's, who's, let's, I've, we've, they've, I'll, and you'll. In addition, an ASCII word ending in n't uses the general rule stem + " not", so didn't, isn't, and shouldn't are covered without separate dictionary entries.

Matching is case-insensitive and occurs on complete ASCII letter/apostrophe tokens. Casing is transferred according to the source form:

Source form

Result policy

Example

lowercase

lowercase expansion

can't -> can not

initial capital

first expansion letter capitalized

Won't -> Will not

all capitals

complete expansion capitalized

CAN'T -> CAN NOT

The method is intentionally lexical rather than grammatical. It does not infer whether 's means is or has, and it does not expand arbitrary possessives or apostrophe-bearing identifiers. A curly apostrophe is not silently treated as a straight apostrophe; call normalize_quotes() or clean() first when input uses typographic punctuation.

No cleanup is bundled into this operation. Surrounding spaces, tabs, line breaks, punctuation, and unaffected words are copied byte-for-byte. That makes the method safe to insert into a pipeline without unexpectedly reflowing text. The result is a fresh, shape-preserving Text Note, and a second application is idempotent because the expanded forms contain no contraction token.

Empty Text Notes remain empty, undefined propagates, and non-Text dtypes are rejected.

Example 1: Dictionary And General n't Forms¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"I can't; You're ready, but they didn't."})
        .nlp().expand_contractions()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["I can not; You are ready, but they did not."]

can't uses a special expansion because its stem is not obtained by merely removing n't; didn't exercises the general suffix rule.

Example 2: Casing And Token Boundaries¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"CAN'T Won't I'M we're shell'code"})
        .nlp().expand_contractions()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["CAN NOT Will not I AM we are shell'code"]

shell'code is one apostrophe-bearing token but not a known contraction, so it is preserved.

Example 3: Whitespace Is Content Here¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"  it's\tstill\nthere  "})
        .nlp().expand_contractions()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["  it is\tstill\nthere  "]

Example 4: A Shape-Preserving Batch¶

const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{" can't ", "12", "“yes”", "plain"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    matrix.nlp().expand_contractions()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  [" can not ", "12"], 
  ["“yes”", "plain"]
]

For empty, undefined, and dtype behavior, the family-wide contract described on clean applies identically. Bytes, Bool, Int64, and Float64 Notes are not interpreted as prose.

See Also¶

  • clean: normalize punctuation and whitespace before expansion.

  • normalize_quotes: convert curly apostrophes without applying the rest of the cleaning pipeline.

  • split_whitespace: produce word-like fields after expansion.
